$comment: Golden cases for the ui.config.ai resolver (GENC-1601 contract C-8). genesis-create owns this file; the seed carries a VERBATIM copy, and each side pins its digest so a change is a deliberate version bump rather than an edit. Every case states WHY it exists — a case whose reason is not obvious is a case someone will 'fix' the day it fails.

cases.name: AI off: nothing is emitted
cases.why: A project that did not select AI chat must generate exactly what it always did — the absence of the block is the contract, not `enabled: false` (C57).

cases.name: A snapshot entity with insert and modify enabled
cases.why: The ordinary case: one readable entity, the two write paths that are on by default, and delete left out because it was never exposed (R-2 a).

ai.systemPrompt: You are an assistant inside the Trading Desk application. Answer questions about its data using the tools you are given, and say so plainly when a question cannot be answered from them. Never state that a record was created, changed or removed unless a tool call confirmed it. A value that must match a row in another table, such as an id, is copied exactly from a row a read tool returned or from a key returned by a confirmed write. Never invent one; if no row matches, say so.

cases.why: Codegen emits a requestReply only for a snapshot-enabled entity or view, so POSITION has no REQ_ to address (C34 — a wrong name fails silently). Delete and custom are opt-in and here they were opted into.

cases.name: A view named after a table yields one request resource, not two
cases.why: Both would derive REQ_TRADE. The chat would tolerate the duplicate; MCP's enableMcp refuses the entire script over one (`require(!enabledResources.containsKey(resource))`), so the whole MCP surface of the generated app dies on a list the preview showed as fine. The supported paths cannot produce this today — getProjectUsedNames (client/src/utils/reserved-names.ts:44) puts entities and views in ONE namespace and both the wizard and the AI tools check it — but a payload can still carry it, and the invariant is cheaper than discovering it at GSF 10.

cases.name: A custom handler named after a generated CRUD one yields one event resource
cases.why: EVENT_TRADE_INSERT from both the entity's enabled insert and a custom handler literally named TRADE_INSERT. This one IS reachable today: the project namespace holds the CRUD handler under its ENTITY key (eventHandlers['TRADE']), so the derived wire name TRADE_INSERT is free for a custom handler to take. The project is already ill-formed at that point — codegen would emit the handler name twice — and the resolver's job is not to fix that but to refuse to compound it into a dead MCP surface.

cases.name: An over-long read is dropped with a warning, and no reference hint points at it
cases.why: FUI blocks the WHOLE assistant when one resource name is over 64 characters (its tool name is the name lowercased, and vendors cap tool names at 64), so a 61-character snapshot table must cost only its own read. The drop has to happen where the reads are built: they decide which references get a hint, and a hint that told the chat to copy a value from REQ_ of a table it cannot read would send it to a tool that does not exist. The 60-character table is the boundary — REQ_ plus 60 is exactly 64, and is kept.
